title: 11 Best Design Agencies in San Francisco
summary: Compare the 11 best design agencies in San Francisco, with every location verified from the agency's own contact page, plus real cost ranges by discipline.
body_markdown:
**Key takeaways:**


- Every location below came from the agency's own contact page, because the directories ranking San Francisco design agencies routinely list firms based elsewhere.
- Federal business data records 33,378 employer establishments in San Francisco County across a population of 826,079, so "design agency" here covers everything from two-person studios to global consultancies.
- Federal occupational data puts the national median for industrial designers at $79,450, and Bay Area rates sit well above it, which is most of why local agency pricing looks steep.
- Decide whether you need product design, brand design or digital design before you compare quotes, because those are three different industries wearing one label.


San Francisco is one of the few cities where you can hire the studio that designed a household product, the firm that invented human-centered design as a discipline, and a two-person data visualization shop, all within a few blocks.


That density is the problem. Searching for a design agency here returns a wall of firms whose homepages read almost identically, and the ranking sites are not much help. We checked, and several agencies listed as San Francisco design firms are in San Mateo, San Jose or Berkeley.


Below are eleven that are genuinely worth a shortlist, sorted by what they actually make. We're first, and we've been direct about where a specialist studio will beat a subscription, including the cases where a matched[designer from a talent bench](https://www.awesomic.com/talent) is the wrong shape for the job.


## Three industries, one job title


"Design agency" in San Francisco covers three largely separate professions, and hiring across the boundary is the most expensive mistake available.


Industrial and product design covers physical objects: hardware, packaging, consumer electronics. Brand and communication design covers identity, campaigns and the visual language a company speaks in. Digital and experience design covers software, websites and interfaces.


A studio that designed an award-winning speaker enclosure is not automatically the right team for your dashboard, and the reverse is equally true. Some firms genuinely span all three, but most lead from one, and the lead discipline shows in the work.


Look at the last five projects on a studio's site rather than its services page. Services pages list ambitions; portfolios show habits.


The third category splits again once you get into it, since[digital design agencies](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/digital-design-agencies) range from marketing-site shops to product teams embedded alongside engineers, and those quote very differently for what sounds like the same brief.


## The 11 best design agencies in San Francisco


The table leads with verified location and lead discipline, the two things that narrow a shortlist fastest. Addresses come from each firm's own site.

Every firm above is inside San Francisco, which took real work to establish. The reasons that mattered are in the verification section further down.


### 1. Awesomic


**Best for:** teams that need design continuously across several surfaces rather than one deep project.


We work from 156 2nd Street with a distributed bench of vetted talent, and we sell design as a monthly subscription rather than a scoped engagement. Send a task, get matched with a suitable designer usually within a day, and keep sending as the work evolves.


The reason that model suits a lot of San Francisco companies is simple: their design demand is not one project, it is a steady stream of landing pages, decks, app screens, launch videos and brand assets, all needing to look like they came from one company.


**Core services:** web and UI/UX design, no-code builds in Webflow and Framer, identity and logo work, decks, packaging, print, motion and video, plus copy and QA on the upper tier.


**How it works:**


1. Send the task with whatever context you have.
2. A designer with the right discipline is assigned, normally within a day.
3. Review and revise in Slack, without a per-round charge.
4. Keep the queue moving as new work appears.


**Pricing:** Graphic Pack sits at $1,490 monthly and All-in-One at $2,995, both discounted a fifth on quarterly terms. Dedicated Talent pairs one full-time creative with a PM, priced case by case.


**Where a studio beats us:** we do not design hardware, and we do not run multi-month research programs with your executive team. For a physical product, talk to Huge Design or Fuseproject. For an organizational redesign, talk to IDEO. Where we compete is breadth and pace on digital and brand work, which is what most companies here actually need most weeks.


Worth a conversation?[Book demo](https://www.awesomic.com/demo) .


### 2. IDEO


**Best for:** organizations that need to change how they operate, not just how they look.


IDEO works from 350 Florida Street with offices including Chicago, and it is the firm most associated with human-centered design as a named practice. Its work reaches beyond artifacts into service design, organizational change and capability building, which is a different purchase from a design project.


**Core services:** human-centered design, service and system design, organizational design, product and digital design.


**Pricing:** no rate card, engagements are consultancy-scale.


**Why it earns a place here:** when the design question is really a strategy question, few firms operate at this level. If you need a website redesigned, this is a mismatch in both scope and budget.


### 3. Fuseproject


**Best for:** ambitious hardware and product launches where the object has to be iconic.


Fuseproject operates from 1401 16th Street and positions on design and innovation for ambitious leaders, with recent work spanning Samsung, TELO Trucks, AES and the ElliQ companion robot. The studio's reputation rests on physical products that define a category rather than iterate within one.


**Core services:** industrial design, brand, digital product, packaging, design strategy.


**Pricing:** no public figures.


**Its real strength:** turning a technically difficult product into something people want to own. It is expensive, project-scoped, and worth it when the object itself is the business.


### 4. Huge Design


**Best for:** companies bringing a physical product to market, at any stage.


Huge Design describes itself as an award-winning industrial design studio in the heart of San Francisco, at 1082 Howard Street, working with entrepreneurs, startups and Fortune 500 companies alike. The tight-knit team framing is meaningful here: you are buying senior attention rather than a large delivery machine.


**Core services:** industrial design, product development, prototyping, design for manufacture.


**Pricing:** no public figures.


**Where it fits:** hardware teams that want experienced industrial designers without a global consultancy's overhead. Purely digital products are outside its lane.


### 5. Manual


**Best for:** companies that need to articulate an ambitious story and look the part.


Manual runs from 2475 Third Street, with a second base in Amsterdam, and calls itself the brand studio for ambitious ideas. Its stated method is helping organizations tell the biggest story they can credibly claim, and it works with category creators and cultural institutions as well as companies entering a new chapter.


**Core services:** brand strategy, visual identity, digital design, campaign and launch work.


**Pricing:** no public figures.


**What it's genuinely good at:** the credibility test built into that positioning. It is a brand studio, so if your need is a product interface you would be hiring the wrong discipline.


### 6. Frog


**Best for:** enterprises running design as part of a wider transformation.


Frog maintains a San Francisco studio within a global network spanning New York, London and beyond, and it now sits inside a large consulting group. That changes what you get: deep capacity and international reach, with the process weight that comes attached.


**Core services:** product and experience design, service design, design strategy, digital transformation.


**Pricing:** enterprise-scoped, no rate card.


**Why buyers shortlist it:** scale and the ability to staff a long program across geographies. A startup needing a fast, opinionated design partner will find the machinery heavy.


### 7. Play Studio


**Best for:** brands that want the identity and the working website from one team.


Play runs from the Mission and keeps a New York outpost, and its distinguishing feature is that the same team designs and then builds. For a design engagement specifically, that means the interface you approve is the interface that ships.


**Core services:** digital product design, web design and front-end build, brand identity.


**Pricing:** no public figures.


**Where it beats the alternatives:** continuity between the design and the code. If you already have engineers, you are paying for capability you may not use.


### 8. Stamen Design


**Best for:** organizations whose core asset is data nobody can read.


Stamen is a San Francisco data visualization and cartography firm in the 94114 zip, and it is one of the few studios anywhere with genuine depth in mapping and large-scale data design. That is a rare, narrow specialism, and when you need it nothing else substitutes.


**Core services:** data visualization, cartography and mapping, interactive data experiences, design research.


**Pricing:** no published rates.


**Its real strength:** clarity at scale. Its work is not a general design service, and for a standard brand or website project you would be pointing a specialist at a generic problem.


### 9. Savas Labs


**Best for:** teams that want strategy, design and engineering from one accountable group.


Savas Labs works from 40 Boardman Place and positions around AI-powered strategy, design, engineering and growth. Combining those under one roof suits organizations that would otherwise hand a design off to a separate development shop and lose intent in translation.


**Core services:** digital strategy, product and web design, engineering, applied AI, growth.


**Pricing:** no public figures.


**Why it made this list:** the end-to-end model with a current AI practice, which is genuinely useful when the thing being designed has a model behind it.


### 10. Gershoni Creative


**Best for:** companies wanting an independent studio for identity and digital work together.


Gershoni has run as an independent San Francisco studio out of 94103 for long enough to have outlasted several design eras. Staying unowned means no network above it setting process or utilization targets, which shows in how much senior time a project actually gets.


**Core services:** design and art direction, identity systems, digital, campaign work.


**Pricing:** no rate card.


**Where it fits:** mid-size projects that need senior attention throughout rather than a pitch team followed by juniors.


### 11. Iron Creative


**Best for:** enterprise brands producing large volumes of content across channels.


Iron operates at the point where design becomes infrastructure, running the component libraries and production pipelines that large e-commerce and B2B organizations depend on to stay consistent. Most of the work is invisible to customers and load-bearing for the brand.


**Core services:** design systems and component libraries, production creative, e-commerce and B2B digital.


**Pricing:** no public figures.


**What to know before hiring:** this is scale work. A small team needing one beautiful thing would be buying governance it has no use for.


## How we verified these eleven


The verification step changed this list more than the research did.


San Francisco County is dense: the Census Bureau's[QuickFacts](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/sanfranciscocountycalifornia/PST045224) puts 33,378 employer establishments inside a population of 826,079. Plenty of design firms genuinely operate here, which makes it easy to assume any agency appearing in a San Francisco ranking is one of them.


They frequently are not. Read a Clutch city listing closely and it commits only to the agency **serving** the metro, which is a statement about sales coverage and not about where anyone sits. Built In SF's design article includes Extractable, whose own site gives San Mateo, while the same publisher files agencies under city neighborhoods that their contact pages contradict with Berkeley and Daly City addresses. A UX roundup we checked listed Eight25Media, which is in San Jose.


Two candidates were worse. One agency domain we followed from a current listing now serves a Dutch-language casino affiliate site; a second serves an Indonesian gambling page. Neither is a design agency any more.


We also dropped good firms rather than guess. One well-regarded studio publishes no location anywhere on its site, and a name we followed from a UX roundup turned out to be a compliance software company at the domain the roundup pointed to. Where we could not confirm a claim, we left the firm out rather than repeat someone else's error.


## What San Francisco design actually costs


Nobody in this tier publishes rates, so the useful thing is understanding the inputs. Labor dominates: federal figures for[industrial designers](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/arts-and-design/industrial-designers.htm) show a $79,450 median in May 2024, and Bay Area salaries run well above the national median before you add overhead and margin.


Engagement Typical range What it buys Best when


Monthly subscription Starts at $1,490 Continuous digital and brand output Demand is steady and varied


Boutique studio project $25,000 to $100,000 A focused identity or product design engagement One defined deliverable


Industrial design program $75,000 to $400,000 Concept through design for manufacture A physical product going to market


Global consultancy $250,000 and up Research, strategy, design, change management The problem is organizational


Our subscription is the one published number here. Everything else reflects how firms in each band talk about their own engagements, so treat it as orientation and get a written quote. If your need is steady output rather than one deep engagement, the comparison worth running is against the models laid out in[design service models](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/top-5-design-service-models-in-2025-pros-cons-and-costs) .


## How to choose between them


Start with the artifact, not the agency.


Physical product? Huge Design and Fuseproject, in that order of budget. Organizational or service problem dressed as a design problem? IDEO. Brand and story? Manual and Gershoni. Brand plus a working site? Play Studio. Data nobody can read? Stamen. Enterprise content sprawl? Iron Creative. Design plus engineering, with AI in the mix? Savas Labs. Running a global program? Frog.


We are the right call when the answer is "all of the digital ones, continuously," which is more common than the project-shaped default assumes. That breadth question usually turns on how many disciplines you need in a given quarter rather than on the quality of any single studio.


Whichever route you take, do the thing that took us the longest here and open each agency's contact page first. It reliably removes a third of any San Francisco shortlist, and among the very[biggest design agencies](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/biggest-design-agencies) it also tells you which office would actually staff your project.


## FAQs


### What does a San Francisco design agency charge?


Rate cards are rare. Boutique studio projects commonly run $25,000 to $100,000, industrial design programs $75,000 to $400,000 depending on manufacturing scope, and global consultancy engagements start around $250,000. Subscriptions are the one tier with a public price, from $1,490 monthly. Rates here sit above national averages because they carry Bay Area salaries; BLS puts the national median for industrial designers at $79,450 as of May 2024.


### Are the agencies in San Francisco directories actually located there?


Frequently not. Clutch's city pages state that an agency serves San Francisco rather than sits in it, and we found current articles placing firms in SF neighborhoods when their own contact pages say Berkeley, Daly City, San Mateo or San Jose. Two domains we followed from live listings now host gambling sites. Open the contact page yourself before assuming anything about location.


### What is the difference between a product design agency and a digital design agency here?


Product design in San Francisco usually means physical objects: hardware, packaging, consumer devices, with prototyping and design for manufacture attached. Digital design means software, websites and interfaces. The words overlap and some firms do both, but the skill sets, tooling and timelines differ substantially, so name the artifact in your first email rather than the discipline. A third group,[graphic design agencies](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/graphic-design-agencies) , handles the print and marketing collateral neither of the first two prioritizes.


### Should I hire a San Francisco agency if my company is elsewhere?


Only if the specific expertise justifies it. Bay Area rates carry Bay Area costs, and for standard brand or web work you can get equivalent quality for less elsewhere, which is why many[mid-market](https://www.awesomic.com/mid-market) teams split the difference by buying local specialism only where it is genuinely scarce. It makes sense when you need hardware design, data visualization at scale, or proximity to your investors and hiring market.


### How long does a design engagement take?


A focused identity or website project runs six to twelve weeks. Industrial design programs run six months to two years once tooling and manufacturing are involved. Consultancy engagements addressing organizational questions run six months and up. Subscriptions invert the shape entirely, shipping continuously from within a day or two rather than delivering at the end, which is the core tradeoff behind buying[design as a service](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/design-as-a-service) instead of a project.
